title: ASEAN adopts first regional space cooperation pact

blocks.text: Leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) have adopted the bloc’s first declaration dedicated exclusively to space cooperation, marking a milestone in regional efforts to advance space science and technology.

The ASEAN Leaders’ Declaration on the Advancement of Space Science, Technology and Innovation Cooperation was spearheaded by the Philippines through the Philippine Space Agency (PhilSA) during the 49th ASEAN Summit.

PhilSA said the declaration reflects the collective commitment of ASEAN member states to strengthen regional collaboration in space science and technology and expand the use of space applications across the region.

“More than a formal statement, this Declaration reflects a shared regional vision to strengthen collaboration in space science, technology, and innovation,” PhilSA Director General Gay Jane Perez said in a press release on Tuesday.

“Through this, we hope to further advance ASEAN’s collective capacity to harness space technologies in support of disaster resilience, environmental sustainability, economic growth, and inclusive development across our region,” she added.
The declaration identifies three key pillars of cooperation: space security and safety, space economy, and space workforce development.
It also aims to promote joint research, expand capacity-building programs, and encourage the sharing of space infrastructure and data among member states.

The declaration recognizes the differences in development levels, technological readiness, institutional capacities, and space capabilities among ASEAN members, while committing to ensure that no member state is left behind through equitable cooperation, capacity building, knowledge sharing, and mutual support.

Signed on Nov. 15, 2026, the declaration was endorsed by all 11 ASEAN member states: Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste, and Vietnam.— MCG, GMA News
